title: StrataTempo: Capacity-Aware Tempo Scorer for Roadmap Prioritization
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Goal: define and prototype a prioritization scorer (StrataTempo) that extends RICE with capacity-awareness, latency/SLO penalties, and cycle-aware urgency (tempo). The intent is to produce a single numeric rank per initiative that (1) surfaces projects that unlock the most product/OKR value per constrained serving capacity, (2) penalizes high-latency or high-cost initiatives unless offset by outsized impact, and (3) adjusts for temporal urgency tied to upcoming cycles and enterprise commitments.

Core intuition: classic RICE misses serving-side constraints and SLA tradeoffs. StrataTempo adds two multiplicative modifiers: a Capacity Factor (captures available GPU capacity / token-econ pressure) and a Tempo Multiplier (captures time sensitivity of the initiative). We also add an SLA Weight that reduces score for initiatives that materially increase latency risk or SLA exposure unless mitigation is included in the plan.
scoring_model:
Components: Reach (R), Impact (I), Confidence (C), Effort (E) — same units as RICE. Capacity Factor (CF): [0.25,1.5] where <1 penalizes capacity-heavy work when pool capacity is constrained. SLA Weight (SW): [0.5,1.0] applied when initiative increases 99th-pct latency or SLA risk. Tempo Multiplier (TM): [0.75,1.5] scales projects by cycle urgency (e.g., strategic enterprise deals => 1.5, long-term research => 0.8).

Formula: Score = ((R * I * C) / max(E, 1)) * CF * SW * TM

Interpretation: higher score = higher priority. CF is computed from a capacity delta model (expected additional tokens/sec demand vs committed capacity); we use an elasticity curve to map demand ratio to [0.25,1.5]. SW defaults to 1.0; set to 0.7 for initiatives that add >5% tail-latency risk without mitigations. TM is set by PM/GTMs based on OKR timing and contractual deadlines.

Example: Initiative A (Adaptive KV cache): R=80, I=3, C=0.8, E=5, CF=1.2 (reduces token cost), SW=1.0, TM=1.1 => Score = ((80*3*0.8)/5)*1.2*1.0*1.1 = 127.5
Initiative B (Large-Model Canary for enterprise): R=20, I=6, C=0.7, E=8, CF=0.7 (adds capacity), SW=0.7 (SLA risk), TM=1.5 (enterprise deadline) => Score = ((20*6*0.7)/8)*0.7*0.7*1.5 = 12.735
acceptance_criteria: Definition doc with scoring inputs, mapping tables for CF and TM, and worked examples (in Confluence) is published and reviewed by Eng and Research.
A lightweight spreadsheet + Python reference implementation that computes scores for existing initiatives in current roadmap.
A demo ranking run comparing current RICE-only ordering vs StrataTempo for the Q2 roadmap with annotated deltas.
Sign-off from Director of Product and Senior Engineering lead on scoring defaults and risk penalties.
Dashboard prototype showing sensitivity (what-if sliders for CF, SW, TM) linked to per-initiative cost/latency estimates.
Runbook for when CF or SW values should be overridden (clear criteria) and an owner assigned.
progress_updates: 2025-02-11: Kickoff with PM, Eng, Research. Aligned on high-level goals; Diego to draft capacity mapping and Ashley (Research) to provide latency risk thresholds.
2025-02-17: First draft of formula reviewed. Engineering requested conservative CF mapping to avoid over-prioritizing token-cost optimizations that add operational complexity.
2025-02-22: Finance provided token-econ curves for Dedicated and Hosted buckets. Incorporated into CF draft; spreadsheet updated.
2025-02-27: Design mocked a dashboard view (score breakdown + sliders). UX suggests adding confidence bands to show sensitivity to C and CF.
2025-03-01: PM review with GTM — tempo multiplier guidelines clarified for enterprise deals and compliance-driven projects. Prepared prototype ranking for leadership review (meeting 2025-03-03).
decisions: Use multiplicative modifiers (CF, SW, TM) instead of additive to keep RICE core intact and preserve diminishing returns logic.
Default SW=1.0; only set <1 when engineering analysis or incident history shows measurable impact to tail latency or SLA exposure.
CF mapping will be conservative by default; higher CF >1 only when initiative reduces expected tokens/sec or materially improves cache hit rates.
Tempo multiplier guidance: 1.5 for contractual deadlines affecting revenue this cycle, 1.2 for cross-org strategic bets, 0.9-0.8 for exploratory work.
tradeoffs: Multiplicative modifiers can amplify noise — we mitigate by bounding modifiers and requiring rationale for overrides.
Adding capacity-awareness favors 'infrastructure' work; to avoid systematic bias, we will normalize CF by initiative type when comparing cross-functional projects.
Tempo multiplier risks gaming by sponsors; mitigate via required GTM justification and leadership sign-off for TM>1.2.
next_steps: Finalize CF mapping table with Eng by 2025-03-07 (Diego) — use Dedicated & Hosted curves and worst-case saturation scenarios.
Deliver Python reference implementation and unit tests (ENG PR) 2025-03-10.

If approved, iterate on UI/Console integration Q2 planning ticket and add rolling adoption plan for PMs.
notes: Related initiatives: this is intended to complement not replace existing RICE reporting. PMs can opt-in to use StrataTempo for Q2 roadmap reviews.
We will pilot on top 30 roadmap candidates to validate scoring stability before broader roll-out.
Engineering requested that any SW <0.8 must include a mitigation plan (autoscaling, fallback model, canary strategy).
